title: Ken Owens and Ian Burns's funeral
summary: Boy-wonder cornettist Ken Owens never developed; pianist Ian Burns died suddenly and the Johnson band played at the graveside.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: What about Ken Owens' band? What was that?

Ken Owens, he was a boy wonder, 16, 17 years old. He was playing beautiful sounding stuff on cornet. He just never developed, unfortunately. He's still occasionally playing very promising sort of stuff, but not, he's just never developed. He's now, he must be in his mid-thirties. He's just never made it. He's around your age, huh? Yes, yes. He, I just can't understand it.
And Ian Burns, is he the one that's playing yet?

No, he, unfortunately, he was a fine pianist, strong sort of honky-tonk sort of style. And, unfortunately, he died suddenly, something caught in his throat or something. Oh. Yes, it was very, he was playing with the Frank Johnson band. And, suddenly, we heard he died at a big funeral for him. We played at the funeral.
The band, didn't it? Yes, Flea's a Bird and all that. At the grave side? Yes, at the grave side.

We didn't want to, or we sort of didn't want to if it was going to affect his relatives at all. You know, they didn't know anything about jazz. But, his wife insisted. Mm-hmm. So, we did it. They were very happy about it. Happy. They were very glad we did it. Mm-hmm.
